contents_summary: ZIP with one 1-page PDF holding Figure S1: two dark-mode phone screenshots from a health app, a heart-rate sample detail on the left and an ECG recording detail on the right, each with sample, source and device detail rows, with the caption printed beneath. The values and date and time stamps are pixel content inside the screenshots and are not extracted as facts.

pages.contents: Page 1: two side-by-side screenshots (heart-rate sample details; ECG recording details) with device detail rows, and the printed caption "Figure S1: Apple Health app data showing sinus bradycardia (left screenshot) followed by ECG recording (right screenshot)." The caption is the only text layer; everything else is image pixels.
pages.clinical_relevance_notes: The screenshots carry device-reported values and date and time stamps as pixels, plus a device-owner name; per the corpus ruling, values printed inside images are not turned into facts. The article text cites this figure for the transient sinus bradycardia during NP sampling and gives no value, so no clinical-data transcription or fact is recorded; the page is attributed to the index patient.
limitations: Burned-in date and time stamps and a device-owner name appear in the screenshots; categories only are recorded here, never their values.
Values read from the screenshots are not extracted as typed facts; no separate page-level rights notice or exception is printed.
Reviewed from the rendered page of the single extracted member PDF; the ZIP contains no other members.
Pixel values in the screenshots are intentionally not transcribed as clinical facts (RULINGS: values inside images stay out of facts).
